original_question: Assume 0 <= alpha < 1, n = 2, and phi is a maximal plurisubharmonic function of class C^{2,alpha}. Determine whether the support of dd^c phi is foliated or laminated by holomorphic discs along which phi is harmonic.
target_in_paper: Question 4 (Dujardin) in §1.1.2, “Maximal plurisubharmonic functions,” pages 4–5: the paper asks, in the local setting and in complex dimension 2, whether a maximal C^{2,alpha} plurisubharmonic function must have supp(dd^c phi) foliated or laminated by holomorphic discs on which phi is harmonic. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s exact unresolved regularity threshold 0 <= alpha < 1, the restriction n = 2, the hypothesis that phi is maximal and plurisubharmonic, and the precise geometric conclusion being asked about: foliation or lamination of supp(dd^c phi) by holomorphic discs along which phi is harmonic. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places the question in the local setting of a domain Omega subset of C^2; this ambient domain is implicit in your draft and should be stated. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, phi should be declared as phi in PSH(Omega) intersect C^{2,alpha}(Omega), not only as a “maximal plurisubharmonic function of class C^{2,alpha}.” ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The notion of maximality should be spelled out exactly as in Definition 1.2: for every v in PSH(Omega) with v <= phi near partial Omega, one has v <= phi on Omega. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The support involved is the support of the positive (1,1)-current or differential form dd^c phi, not the support of the Monge-Ampere measure (dd^c phi)^2. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The discs should be identified as holomorphic discs Delta_t contained in Omega, and the intended meaning of harmonicity is that the restriction phi|_{Delta_t} is harmonic on each such disc. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To stay paper-faithful, the wording should remain an open yes/no problem (“Is ...?” or “Must ...?”), rather than “Determine whether,” which can sound like the paper proves the answer. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

No extra DMA(Omega), boundedness, compact-Kahler, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency assumptions belong to this question; the paper asks it exactly for arbitrary maximal psh phi with C^{2,alpha} regularity in the local n = 2 setting. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let Omega be a domain in C^2, let 0 <= alpha < 1, and let phi belong to PSH(Omega) intersect C^{2,alpha}(Omega). Assume phi is maximal in Omega, meaning that whenever v belongs to PSH(Omega) and v <= phi near partial Omega, then v <= phi throughout Omega. Must the support of the positive current dd^c phi be foliated—or at least laminated—by holomorphic discs Delta_t subset Omega such that the restriction phi|_{Delta_t} is harmonic on each disc? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: it is exactly Question 4 (Dujardin) in §1.1.2, not a broader neighboring problem. Definition 1.2 provides the hidden definition of “maximal,” which your draft leaves implicit. The paragraph immediately preceding Question 4 explains why the paper isolates the C^{2,alpha} threshold: a holomorphic-disc foliation implies maximality; in dimension 2, a C^3 maximal psh function has supp(dd^c phi) foliated by such discs via Frobenius; and Dujardin exhibited C^{1,alpha} maximal examples with no such holomorphic disc. So the sharp paper-faithful research question is exactly the local C^{2,alpha}, n = 2 converse problem, with no added global or DMA assumptions. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
